correctness_confidence.basis: All four theorems, Lemma 1, Eqs. (2)-(6), and numerical thresholds in Table 1 were independently verified. Theorem 1's diagonal and adjacent-swap deduplication, Lemma 1's three-case bad-subarray run bound, and Theorem 2's three-tier packing inequality are mathematically sound, with no errors found.

rigor.basis: Proofs are concise and valid across all cases, carefully evaluating run counts on deleted slices X^(-j) and X^(-i) to avoid projection run-collapse. Minor proof compression occurs in Theorem 1 (injectivity of swap pairs is implicit), and Lean 4 formalizes supporting lemmas T01-T20 while Lemma 1 and Eqs. (3)-(4) remain paper proofs.

novelty.basis: Genuinely proves strictly sharper non-asymptotic bounds beyond Li-Sun-Ge (arXiv:2611.34447v1): exact indel-pair deduplication (up to 4x in binary) and a three-tier deleted-slice run decomposition lowering strict binary thresholds from n>=27 to n>=18. However, leading asymptotics are unchanged and Theorems 3-4 are elementary.

significance.basis: Strictly closes a sizable finite-length gap (n in [18, 26] for q=2, plus reductions for q=3,4,5) and extends the sphere-packing converse to rectangular m x n arrays. Practical impact is moderate since the asymptotic redundancy rate is unchanged, n in [3, 17] remains open, and no new code constructions are given.

reproducibility.basis: Provides exact rational formulas, explicit parameter choices (s values and threshold pairs), SHA-256 artifact digests, Lean 4.36.0 theorem inventory (T01-T20), and exact-Q certificate summaries (C01-C16) matching independent recalculation.

summary: This manuscript strictly sharpens the non-asymptotic sphere-packing converse of Li, Sun, and Ge (arXiv:2611.34447v1) for q-ary (1,1)-criss-cross deletion-correcting codes. By deduplicating diagonal and adjacent-transposition collisions in single-insertion balls (Theorem 1) and refining the bad-subarray lemma across all three deletion-collision cases onto deleted slices to enable a three-tier packing decomposition (Lemma 1 and Theorem 2), the author reduces the overhead term epsilon by 53.3x-90.2x in binary and lowers the strict finite-length redundancy threshold r_C > 2n + 2 log_q n - 2 from n >= 27 to n >= 18 (q=2), 15 to 11 (q=3), 11 to 9 (q=4), and 9 to 8 (q=5), while extending the converse to rectangular m x n arrays (Theorem 3) and computing exact binary capacities for 2x2 and 2x3 arrays (Theorem 4).
strengths: Theorem 1 provides a clean, exact algebraic improvement over Li-Sun-Ge Lemma 6 by factor q^2/(q-1)^2 (4x in binary) with exact equality at L=2.

Lemma 1 cleanly refines Case 3 of Li-Sun-Ge Lemma 5 to show that every bad codeword contributes at least rho_row(X^(-j)) - 2 or rho_col(X^(-i)) - 2 bad subarrays, while correctly evaluating run counts on deleted slices to prevent projection run-collapse.
Theorem 2's s-parameterized three-tier packing bound yields large verified finite-length threshold improvements across q in {2, 3, 4, 5} and generalizes cleanly to rectangular m x n arrays.
Transparent verification boundary separating Lean 4.36.0 formalized lemmas (T01-T20), exact-Q rational computations (C01-C16), and out-of-scope directions.
weaknesses: Leading asymptotic redundancy 2n - 1 + 2 log_q n - o_q(1) is unchanged from Li-Sun-Ge [3], the small binary regime n in [3, 17] remains open, and no new code constructions are provided.

Theorem 3 Part 1 merely restates Theorem 2 for rectangular dimensions, while Theorem 3 Part 2 is an elementary fixed-position 2D parity-check bijection (which solves erasures at known (r,c) rather than unknown criss-cross deletions).
Theorem 4 is a tiny exact calculation (64 arrays on 2x3, where |C*(2,2,3)|=2 also follows from a two-line pigeonhole argument on length-3 binary words) that adds limited mathematical depth.

Lean 4 formalization covers 20 structural list/algebraic lemmas and finite rational checks (T01-T20) rather than an end-to-end formalization of Lemma 1's 2D subarray case analysis or the counting bounds (3)-(4), though Section 3 transparently discloses this.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact Levenshtein diagonal-and-swap deduplicated single-indel confusable pair bound P_indel(q, L) <= q^(L-1)(L^2(q-1)^2 + 2q - 1) (Theorem 1).

Deleted-slice bad-ball lower bound (Lemma 1) and three-tier run-decomposed sphere-packing converse (Theorem 2), lowering strict finite-length redundancy thresholds from n >= 27 to n >= 18 for q=2 and improving q=3,4,5 and rectangular m x n regimes.
